headlines.title: Anthropic tells IPO investors it could be targeted over its AI safety views
Nevis, which uses AI to automate paperwork for financial advisors, raised a $70M Series B led by EQT Ventures, a source says at a $500M valuation (Camila Grigera Naón/Fortune)
Bedrock Robotics, which makes driverless excavators and other autonomous construction machines, raised a $600M Series C at a $4.1B valuation (Edward Ludlow/Bloomberg)
Few VC firms are mentioned in Anthropic's S-1, except Spark, which invested ~$800M across six rounds and whose GP Yasmin Razavi is the sole VC on its board (Kate Clark/Wall Street Journal)
S-1: Anthropic warns prospective investors that its AI safety and advocacy stances risk disproportionate and selective targeting from the Trump administration (Maria Curi/Axios)
Anthropic’s IPO filing lays out a plan to ‘revolutionize every area of human endeavor’ with AI

Apple’s new iPad mini gets OLED, an A20 Pro chip and water resistance
‘Not a new AI center’: Seattle Children’s launches $10M pediatric innovation institute
Nevis raises $70M to expand its AI platform for wealth advisers
Sources: Anthropic is aiming to go public the week of November 16 and could raise ~$100B at a $1.5T to $2T valuation, after initially preparing for October (Wall Street Journal)
Anthropic's S-1 lists 94 pages of risk factors and warns that the "scale of harm" from a "catastrophic" AI incident might mean it is unable to obtain insurance (Wall Street Journal)
California Startups Have Raised More So Far In 2026 Than The Entire US Ever Has In A Single Year
Evertrace acquires Veck to strengthen early founder detection
Etzioni on AI: $137M spent on AI-generated midterm ads, and most voters can’t spot the fakes
S-1: as of September 30, Anthropic had 11,900+ customers spending $100,000+ annually, 1,900+ customers spending $1M+, and ~250 customers spending $10M+ (Rebecca Bellan/TechCrunch)
Microsoft and others push out emergency patches for a critical flaw in Brotli, the C decoder library built into Node.js, that could allow remote code execution (Bill Toulas/BleepingComputer)
